questions.q: What is the real tradeoff every layer (staging, intermediate, marts) imposes on a project?
options: Overhead — each layer is a file that must be written, reviewed, tested, and understood by the next engineer
Extra warehouse storage costs only, with no effect on people
A mandatory license fee per layer in dbt Cloud
Slower query performance at read time, with no other cost
questions.explain: Layering is not free — it's a bet that dividing work into files pays for itself once a project has enough real complexity to need it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what actually goes wrong with 'one big model' as a project grows?
options: Every future change requires understanding the entire tangled file, because renaming, joins, and business logic were never separated
dbt refuses to compile a model above a certain line count
One big model always produces incorrect results immediately
The warehouse charges more to store one large model than several small ones
questions.explain: One big model can even be correct at first — the real cost shows up later, when any single change requires re-verifying everything at once.

questions.q: Why does adding a fifth layer 'for extra safety' also fail, according to this lesson?
options: More structure doesn't automatically add clarity — a small project with a fifth layer just adds files to open without adding insight
dbt technically enforces a maximum of three layers per project
A fifth layer is always slower to query than four layers
Five layers is only a problem if the project has fewer than three models
questions.explain: This is the same 'narrow the DAG, widen the tables' principle from Lesson 14 — extra hops that don't do a genuine job just add friction.

questions.q: What is 'the layer test' this lesson proposes for deciding whether a layer belongs?
options: Does this model do one clear job that the layer above or below it can't do as well?
Does this model have at least five columns?
Is this model referenced by more than three other models?
Was this model created in the last sprint?
questions.explain: If a model exists only because 'that's where models go,' rather than doing a distinct job, it fails the test and is the wrong kind of layer.

questions.q: According to this lesson, is it ever correct for a small project to skip the intermediate layer entirely?
options: Yes — intermediate exists only when marts would otherwise need it, so going straight from staging to marts on a simple project is correct, not incomplete
No — every dbt project must have exactly three layers regardless of size
No — skipping intermediate always causes test failures
Yes, but only if the project has zero staging models
questions.explain: Three layers is the right default, not a fixed rule — a small project with simple joins can skip intermediate and go straight from staging to marts.
